title: stream-qos-billing-aware-tool-calls-prd-draft
summary: Sketch of a Hosted API addition that lets SDKs and the runtime negotiate QoS lanes for streaming calls that invoke external tools, while surfacing per-tool billing signals and cost-aware fallback policies. Focus: predictable latency for high-priority flows, transparent cost attribution, and ergonomic SDK surfaces for developers to opt into QoS tiers and per-call billing hints.
problem_statement: Teams building product features with streaming responses and tool calls face two recurring issues: (1) unpredictable tail latency when tool calls are serialized/blocked by heavy background throughput, and (2) unclear per-call billing / cost attribution when model tokens, tool execution, and external network calls are bundled into a single opaque invoice. Current hosted-api streaming surface lacks a first-class way to express and enforce QoS priorities for tool calls and to retrieve cost breakdowns per logical call. This makes it hard to build low-latency interactive features that also track unit economics accurately.
goals:
- Provide an API-level mechanism to indicate per-request QoS (latency-critical vs batchable) that the runtime will honor across routing/batching and tool execution layers.
- Produce per-request cost breakdowns that isolate model compute vs tool execution vs network egress, surfaced in SDK responses and Console.
- Offer an ergonomic SDK pattern so developers can mark streaming segments and tool calls with QoS hints without heavyweight plumbing.
- Enable cost-aware fallback policies: automatic substitution to cheaper tool variants or model fallbacks when cost thresholds or capacity constraints are hit.
- Maintain backward compatibility: default behavior should match current API for existing clients.
non_goals: - This PRD is not proposing a new billing SKU or major pricing overhaul; focus is on attribution and telemetry.\n- Not addressing on-prem / Private control-plane billing plumbing (that lives in Private product).\n- Not designing new payment or invoicing UI in Console (Console work will be a separate follow-up).
success_metrics:
- 40% reduction in P99 latency for labeled latency-critical streaming flows in customer pilot.
- Per-request cost breakdown accuracy within 5% vs ground-truth internal accounting for pilot workloads.
- SDK adoption: 3 pilot customers integrate QoS hints in first 8 weeks.
- Fallback usage: when fallback policies enabled, cost savings >= 15% with <3% degradation in end-user satisfaction for pilot scenarios.
api_surface:
Proposal: Extend the streaming API with optional QoS & billing hint fields. Backwards compatible — fields are optional.

New top-level request fields (stream / non-stream same semantics):
- qos: string ("latency", "standard", "economy") — hint to runtime about scheduling and placement.
- tool_budget_usd: string (e.g. "0.50") — optional per-request maximum spend for tool executions aggregated. Runtime will attempt to enforce by dropping/deggrading tool calls or selecting cheaper tool variants.
- cost_breakdown: boolean — if true, server returns a structured cost breakdown in final event and as telemetry.
- tool_call_annotations: list of strings — freeform tags to help map which logical tool calls correspond to product features for the customer.

Streaming behavior: QoS hint applies to the whole request by default. SDKs can annotate subframes with "qos:latency" to request elevated lane for that segment (e.g., user-facing clarification messages). Runtime will treat inline segment hints as preemptible markers for scheduling heuristics.

Response additions: When cost_breakdown=true, server emits a final jsonl 'cost_summary' frame containing fields (model_tokens_usd, tool_exec_usd, network_usd, total_usd). This is also emitted as a non-streamed response header for non-stream calls.

Error handling: If tool_budget_usd is exceeded mid-stream, runtime returns a 'tool-budget-exceeded' terminal frame and a recommended action (e.g. "retry-without-tool" or "degraded-result-included").
sdk_ergonomics:
Principles: low friction, minimal breaking changes, idiomatic for JS/TS and Python SDKs, helpers for common patterns.

JS example sketch (streaming):
const stream = client.stream.create({ model: 'rtdx-3b', qos: 'latency', tool_budget_usd: '0.25', cost_breakdown: true });
stream.on('tool-call:start', (meta) => { /* show spinner */ });
stream.on('tool-call:end', (meta) => { /* annotate UI with cost info per tool_call meta.cost */ });
stream.on('cost_summary', (cost) => { console.log(cost); });

Python sync example (non-stream):
resp = client.generate(model='rtdx-3b', qos='economy', tool_budget_usd='0.10', cost_breakdown=True)
print(resp.cost_summary)

SDK responsibilities:
- Expose simple enums/typed hints for QoS.
- Surface incremental tool-call events to let apps show progress and partial costs.
- Provide helpers to translate tool_call_annotations into telemetry tags and Console mappings.
- Transparent fallback toggles: client-side flag to allow runtime to auto-fallback; SDK exposes decision reason in response (e.g., "fallback:cheap-tool-selected").

Backward compatibility: omit new fields to preserve current flows. Helper migration docs + one-line toggles for experimental customers.
billing_model:
This PRD does not change pricing but surfaces per-call credits. Implementation notes: runtime will attribute costs using the following internal mapping:
- model_tokens_usd: computed via per-model per-token unit cost multiplied by tokens consumed.
- tool_exec_usd: includes compute, provider fees, and an attribution fraction for network/service costs.
- network_usd: explicit egress & third-party API costs where measurable.

Output: the cost_summary emitted to customers is a best-effort attribution string. Exact numbers are labeled as 'estimated' until Finance signs off on a certified attribution method. We will route 'tool_exec_usd' through our existing usage pipeline so consumption appears in billing exports; cost_breakdown is for visibility and may be used to drive automatic policy enforcement (tool_budget_usd).

Policy enforcement: tool_budget_usd is a soft limit implemented by the routing layer. If exceeded, runtime can:
- Reject further tool calls and emit a budget-exceeded frame, or
- Downgrade to a cheaper tool variant (if available) and flag fallback reason, or
- Continue but mark response with final warning and let the invoice reflect true cost (opt-in via SDK flag).

Audit trail: each tool-call event will contain a correlation id and provider reference for reconciling third-party charges (string fields surfaced in telemetry).
telemetry_and_observability:
Minimum telemetry events to implement:
- request.received (qos, annotations, tool_budget_usd)
- tool.call.start (tool_id, qos_lane, correlation_id)
- tool.call.end (tool_id, duration_ms, cost_est_usd, success/failure)
- request.cost_summary (model_tokens_usd, tool_exec_usd, network_usd, total_usd)
- request.fallback_taken (reason, replaced_tool_id)

Console: add per-request drilldown to show top N tool calls and approximate cost per tool. Allow filtering by qos lane and annotation tags.

Bench/telemetry experiments: run synthetic tests with mixed traffic to validate QoS lane isolation. Measure head-of-line blocking, P95/P99 per-lane, and cost attribution variance.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal): implement prototype in runtime + instrumented SDKs for internal teams.
Phase 1 (pilot): invite 2–3 customers (embedding-heavy search app, chat product with tool calls) to opt into QoS hints and cost_breakdown. Monitor latency & cost numbers for 6 weeks.
Phase 2 (gradual): enable documented SDKs and console drilldowns for general availability behind an "opt-in" flag. Collect feedback and iterate.
Phase 3: GA — flip opt-in to default for 'cost_breakdown' off, but QoS hints honored; enable billing exports integration after Finance signoff.

Rollout safety: default to "standard" QoS for existing clients. Fallback behavior must be clearly signaled to customers (frames + SDK flags).
open_questions:
- How do we reconcile tool_exec_usd with third-party provider invoices in a way Finance will accept for official billing exports? (Action: eng + finance alignment).
- Should QoS hints be a free-form numeric priority instead of 3 buckets? Tradeoff: flexibility vs simplicity.
- Do we need per-subframe separate budgets (tool_budget_usd per-tool-call) or is a single request budget sufficient for pilot?
- How aggressive should automatic downgrades be if budget exceeded — silent downgrade vs explicit rejection?
- Are there regulatory/compliance concerns with exposing estimated cost breakdowns for enterprise customers?
